title: Átmiton Theory: Elementary Particles as Local Area Networks, with Candidate Structures for the Standard Model, Dark Matter and Dark Energy
content: Particle/field duality is visualized by a local area network (LAN): one public address and point of contact make it appear point-like, while internal topology governs interactions. Guided by this analogy, we model particles and Space as networks of fundamental nodes—átmita—whose addresses, signaling protocol and finite memory govern connectivity and motion. Embedding a particle LAN in Space then has two consequences. First, it creates connection defects whose steady diffusion around a spherical source, combined with memory-budget equilibrium, recovers the first-order weak-field Schwarzschild geometry. Second, the embedding protocol reflects internal addresses along one of three symmetric local bases. Under stated symmetry assumptions, identifying two bases with Dark Energy and the third with matter gives ΩDE → 2/3; matter’s internal reflection variants yield an approximately 80% Dark-Matter share. The growing hidden-basis router population yields a conditional flat FRW-like expansion and the standard redshift law. Temporary basis switching provides a qualitative tunneling mechanism with exponential barrier-width suppression. The resulting sixteen-member catalogue of regular matter systems spans first-generation Standard-Model matter, gauge/Higgs and graviton candidates, and two unassigned structures. A primitive internal cycle supplies spin and rest-mass ansätze; an operational relativity principle yields Lorentz kinematics. A consolidated register lists assumptions, conditional results and open consistency tests.
